rich_summary: This section recounts the dark origin of Parashurama’s wrath against the warrior caste. Renuka, wife of the sage Jamadagni, momentarily feels desire upon seeing King Chitraratha sporting in the water. Jamadagni, perceiving her lapse in chastity, orders his sons to kill her; only Rama obeys, beheading his mother. Pleased with his obedience, Jamadagni grants Rama boons, allowing Renuka and his brothers to be restored and the sin erased. Later, the arrogant sons of Kartavirya steal the sacred cow from the hermitage. Rama kills their mighty leader, but in revenge they murder Jamadagni while he is absorbed in penance. Grief‑stricken, Rama vows annihilation of the Kshatriyas, slaughtering them repeatedly and filling Samantapanchaka with lakes of blood before renouncing the earth and retiring to penance.

highlight_spans.why: Renuka’s sudden desire after seeing the king begins the tragic chain of events and introduces the theme of chastity and transgression.
Jamadagni commands his sons to kill their mother, a shocking test of obedience and ascetic severity central to the legend of Parashurama.
Rama obeys instantly and beheads his mother, the pivotal act that earns him boons and establishes his fierce commitment to duty.
Rama returns to find his father murdered and laments bitterly, the emotional turning point that drives his vow of vengeance.
The account of Rama exterminating the Kshatriyas and creating lakes of blood at Samantapanchaka highlights the epic scale and mythic consequences of his vow.

top_scenes.scene_text: Renuka standing waist‑deep in a river, gazing at King Chitraratha sporting with his queens while lotus garlands float on the water.
Parashurama grimly raising his axe in the forest hermitage as Jamadagni orders him to strike down his own mother.
The battlefield of Samantapanchaka where Parashurama stands amid fallen warriors as five lakes of blood spread across the plain.
